 5. Santorini (2 days),

 7. Seville (5 days) – with Seville (which only connects to Dublin) as the other endpoint.

Using the rule that when you fly from one city to the next the flight day is counted in both cities, the day ranges work out as follows:

• City 1: Vilnius starts Day 1 and lasts 3 days – so Vilnius is Day 1–3.
  (Flight from Vilnius to Frankfurt happens on Day 3, which is counted in both.)

• City 2: Frankfurt lasts 5 days starting on the flight day (Day 3) so its range is Day 3–7.
  (Flight from Frankfurt to Stuttgart happens on Day 7.)

• City 3: Stuttgart lasts 3 days starting on Day 7 giving Day 7–9.
  (This meets the requirement to visit relatives in Stuttgart between Day 7 and Day 9. Flight from Stuttgart to London happens on Day 9.)

• City 4: London lasts 2 days starting on Day 9 so its range is Day 9–10.
  (This ensures you’re in London on Day 9 (and through Day 10) to meet your friends as required.) 
  (Flight from London to Santorini happens on Day 10.)

• City 5: Santorini lasts 2 days beginning on Day 10 so it is visited Day 10–11.
  (Flight from Santorini to Dublin happens on Day 11.)

• City 6: Dublin lasts 3 days starting on Day 11 so its range is Day 11–13.
  (Flight from Dublin to Seville happens on Day 13.)

• City 7: Seville lasts 5 days starting on Day 13 so its range is Day 13–17.

Note that the sum of the individual durations is 23 days. However, because there are 6 flights and each flight day is counted twice (once at the end of one city’s visit and once as the start of the next city), the overall trip is 23 – 6 = 17 days.
